paragraphs.text: As it were between hope and despair he bursts forth into this affection, being assured that God would continue his favour toward such as were godly indeed, and not hypocrites.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: The wicked in this life live at pleasure and are not drawn to death like prisoners: that is, by sickness which is death's messenger.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: They glory in their pride as some do in their chains, and in cruelty, as some do in apparel.
paragraphs.label: c
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore pride compasseth them about as

paragraphs.text: They blaspheme God, and do not fear his power and rail upon men, because they esteem themselves above all others.
paragraphs.label: d
paragraphs.anchor: set their mouth against the heavens

paragraphs.text: Not only the reprobate, but also the people of God often fall back seeing the prosperous estate of the wicked, and are overwhelmed with sorrows, thinking that God does not correctly consider the estate of the godly.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: Thus the flesh moves even the godly to dispute with God concerning their poor estate, and the prosperity of the wicked.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: If I give place to this wicked thought, I offend against your providence, seeing you do all things most wisely and preserve your children in their greatest dangers.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: Until I entered into your school and learned by your word and Holy Spirit that you order all things most wisely and justly.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: When you open our eyes to consider your heavenly happiness, we contemn all their vain pomp.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: For the more that man goes about by his own reason to seek out God's judgments, the more he declares himself a beast.
paragraphs.label: l

paragraphs.text: By faith I was assured that your providence always watched over me to preserve me.
paragraphs.label: m

paragraphs.text: He sought neither help nor comfort of any save God only.
paragraphs.label: n

paragraphs.text: He teaches us to deny ourselves, to have God our whole sufficiency, and only contentment.
paragraphs.label: o

paragraphs.text: That is, forsake you to seek others.
paragraphs.label: p

paragraphs.text: Though all the world shrinks from God, yet he promises to trust in him and to magnify his works.
paragraphs.label: q
